t: Marsyas was a sculpture by Anish Kapoor, made with Cecil Balmond, shown in Tate Modern's Turbine Hall in 2003. It was 150 metres long and ten storeys high, and it was the first commission in the Unilever Series to use the entire hall. It is no longer on show. Its title refers to Marsyas, the satyr in Greek mythology who was flayed alive by the god Apollo. Balmond, an engineer, had joined Ove Arup and Partners in 1968.
